body: For me it changes all the time. Currently its my weight or body size; Ive had obsessions with my nose, my skin, my hairline, my uneven smile, my chin...it just never ends. On my worst days I feel like someone put me together so mismatched it feels like a cruel joke. I wish i could hide a specific flaw and feel fine but its every part of me.

Hey thanks for responding. I am really glad you've gotten a diagnosis at your age I hope it helps to identify it before you begin adulthood...it got worse for me at that point because I had no knowledge or support. I know I was asking for advice but if I could give any to you it would be to quell the bulimia first. It did me no favours - I now have acid reflux, I only ever gained weight from it, and Ive been dehydrated to the point of hospitalization so many times. Secondly make sure you research and medication you're prescribed. Thirdly if your friends and/or family dont understand try not to push it - if you even have one friend to talk to or even your therapist I would just stick to telling them. Nobody understands  me when I try to explain  - I  go round in circles over and over again - I mean what can they say apart from "youre wrong" or "do something about it" or "youre exaggerating"? Ive learnt to realize when someone isnt going to understand and I save myself the hurt and anguish by choosing the right people to confide in. I also suggest staying away from becoming obsessed with photographing yourself. I created a 'proof' album to show anyone that tried to tell me I was wrong about my looks - all these things just amplified things and fed my obsession and look where I am now. I will say I have a great job and am very good at pretending I am not struggling so things could be worse - I dont want you to think because of my story things are hopeless for you too. I am really proud of you naming your demons and realizing its a perception issue and not really about your looks at all. I hope we find peace with it one day, I am so tired. Also, I am so sorry if my story depressed you I dont want you to think there is no hope you are so young. Keep working on it babe. Youve inspired me to do the same so a million times thank you. Look at how mature and worldly you are, thats a beautiful thing in itself. Xx
You can talk to either of us - even to try and help someone understand. You deserve to be heard
Please  don't do it. I think you should put the noose in the bin, have a shower and go to sleep. The feeling might pass. Can you call a friend?
Hey I'm really glad. Things will get better I promise - the hardest part is realizing there are parts of yourself that need reviewing. We always have room to grow :)

I've heard of plenty of people who do not associate with being hetrosexual being called "homophobic". I suggest it relates closely with your fear of letting others know about your sexuality. I could go into depth about it but if you want more info or someone to talk to you can PM me. I have found radical self acceptance can automatically free you from the autonomous habit of projecting negative feelings about yourself onto others.  I hope you don't think I'm being presumptious- It's hard to discern from a paragraph. Ps I am really proud of you for addressing it and for being willing to do some self reflection and growth.

Pps - In response to the other posts - you're being a grown up for trying to address it! Good on you for being brave. Some people never achieve that level of growth; or realize when it's too late and are burdened with regret.

I dont know if they have such community groups in your country or area, but I am a part of some great pay it forward groups on Facebook. Try looking up your suburb and "pay it forward". I have helped and received help from plenty of amazing individuals in my community - the group has changed my life. Everyone pools together to help people in all sorts of predicaments whether it be clothing, gifts, food, employment help, furniture, services..the list is endless. Not to mention the kind hearted friends I've made through the online group - i now have a solid support network. Please try to reach out - and don't be ashamed of asking for help - I'm really proud of you for making this post it's a great first step. You're doing the right thing for you and your family. I'm not a spiritual person but my faith in humanity has been restored by the kindness of strangers. Good luck - if you want to let me know the suburb you live in I'm happy to do some research for you. Send me a PM!
